anchor_definition: The anchor is the login submit handler callback (the 1.json answer, login.js): it assembles the request payload o = {account, password: this.encode(this.encrypt(this.form.password)), areaCode: this.encode(...), extend: this.encode(...)} and posts it via this.login(o). Graded below it on the password path: u (this.encrypt — AES-ECB/Pkcs7 with the fixed key G3JH98Y8MY9GWKWG, then encodeURIComponent(base64), the target-specific ciphertext constructor) 0.7; the URL-encode utility this.encode (encodeURIComponent, reused for password/areaCode/extend) 0.5. Off-chain (0): the inverse decrypt p. NOTE: a clean 0.2 sink is not isolable here — this.login is a Vuex mapped action and the AES math is cross-file CryptoJS.

anchor.why: The login submit handler recorded as the 1.json answer: it builds the request payload o = {account, password: this.encode(this.encrypt(this.form.password)), areaCode, extend, ...} and posts it via this.login(o). The field-binding that produces the observed password ciphertext lives here (password = encode(encrypt(password))).

roles.why: this.encrypt (u): AES-ECB(Pkcs7) of the plaintext with the fixed site key G3JH98Y8MY9GWKWG, then encodeURIComponent(base64). The target-specific password ciphertext constructor nested below the submit handler.

this.encode (I = function(t){return encodeURIComponent(t)}): the generic URL-encode utility applied by callback to the encrypted password and to areaCode/extend. A reusable encoding primitive on the construction path.
this.decrypt (p): the inverse AES decrypt. Opposite direction; not on the request-construction path. A sibling decoy.
